newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon says China Eastern still Hold.
newsitem.headline: Salomon says China Eastern still Hold.

text.p: A 1996 full year earnings review of China Eastern Airlines has retained a Hold rating as analysts believe shares are fully valued at the current price, a new report by Salomon Brother said.

Salomon added that it has slightly adjusted its profit forecast for the airline. The 1997 net profit forecast remains unchanged at 657 million yuan but the 1998 forecast has been "trimmed" from 814 million yuan to 791 million yuan.

The report dated May 6 said the airline's 1996 full-year profit of 591 million yuan reported on April 30 was 6.8 percent below the 1995 result but 4.6 percent above Salomon's estimate of 565 million yuan. The carrier reported a pre-tax profit of 830 million yuan, slightly below Salomon's forecast of 843 million yuan.

Salomon said the result highlighted some dramatic operational changes in China Eastern's business. Domestic traffic revenues increased by 28 percent in 1996 due to a "meagre" 0.1 percent increase in revenue passenger kilometres (RPK offset by a 29.6 percent increase in yields.

Domestic capacity increased by 10 percent resulting in a decline in domestic load factors to 69.5 percent in 1996 from 76.5 percent in 1995. Domestic cargo revenues increased at the slower rate of 14 percent, the report said.

International traffic revenues increased by only 0.8 percent in 1996 hiding a major shift in international operations, the report added. RPK growth was 35.2 percent, marginally exceeding capacity growth of 34.4 percent. International load factors improved from 62.3 percent in 1995 to 62.7 percent in 1996.

"We believe this is an impressive effort considering the extent of the business growth. However, this growth was achieved at the expense of a substantial yield decline of 22.6 percent," the report said.
Hong Kong regional traffic revenues grew by only 1.3 percent in 1996 reflecting operational constraints at Kai Tak airport which has limited traffic growth on many China routes.

The report said the airline will benefit from further domestic yield increases due to the unification of China's previously two-tiered domestic air fare structure and an expected exchange gain from the restatement of the company's yen liabilities.

Salomon also expects the carrier to complete an A share issue in the third quarter with the new funds used to improve the company's balance sheet. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
